country.evidence_quote: Karl-Erik was born in the parish of Edsvära in Västergötland, in the southwest Sweden. He completed his Master in Business and Economics at the Stockholm School of Economics (SSE) in 1950. Karl-Erik then continued doing research at SSE, while at the same time studying psychology and sociology at what later became Stockholm University (at that time Högskolan i Stockholm). internal_collaboration.evidence_quote: The main building on Sveavägen, opened in 1925, is the center of student life and academic activity. It houses lecture halls, study areas, the SSE Library, and common spaces for students and faculty. Over time, the campus has expanded with nearby annex buildings on Saltmätargatan, Holländargatan and Norrtullsgatan that provide additional classrooms, offices, and study spaces within walking distance.

Campus Kämpasten, SSE’s conference and meeting center in Sigtuna, complements the Stockholm campus. It is used for executive education, conferences, and academic gatherings, providing an environment for focused work, discussion, and collaboration.
